title: HTML and CSS Basics
description: Elements, selectors and the box model: the building blocks of web pages

questions.question: What does HTML stand for?
questions.explanation: HTML stands for HyperText Markup Language, the standard language for structuring web pages.

questions.question: Which HTML element creates a hyperlink?
questions.explanation: The <a> (anchor) element creates links, with the destination in its href attribute. <link> connects resources such as stylesheets.

questions.question: Which HTML element holds the largest default heading?
questions.explanation: <h1> is the top-level heading and <h6> the smallest. <head> holds page metadata, not visible headings.

questions.question: Which attribute provides alternative text for an image?
questions.explanation: The alt attribute describes the image for screen readers and is shown if the image fails to load.

questions.question: Which CSS property changes the text color of an element?
questions.explanation: The color property sets text color. font-color and text-color are not CSS properties.

questions.question: Which CSS selector targets an element with id="main"?
questions.explanation: # selects by id and . selects by class. A bare 'main' selects <main> elements.

questions.question: In the CSS box model, which area lies between the content and the border?
questions.explanation: Moving outward from the center the box model goes content, padding, border, margin.

questions.question: Which CSS display value turns an element into a flex container?
questions.explanation: display: flex makes an element a flex container, laying out its children along a main axis.

questions.question: What does CSS stand for?
questions.explanation: CSS means Cascading Style Sheets. 'Cascading' refers to how rules from several sources combine and override each other.

questions.question: Which HTML element should wrap the main navigation links of a page?
questions.explanation: <nav> is the semantic element for major navigation blocks, and it helps assistive technology find them.
